research_concepts: separability of coverage from player talent and minutes counts
possession-level play-type records derived from play-by-play
methodological_questions: Can lineup role coverage be defined operationally from the play-type records without using points or outcomes that the test then predicts?
Is coverage separable from talent proxies and from minutes/exposure counts at the lineup and team-season levels?
Does talent control behave (adequate adjustment, no collinearity with coverage) given available talent proxies?
Do exposure sparsity, measure reliability, and derived-label dependence threaten any test of within-team variation?
evidence_establishes: The historical retrieval returned no records, so no earlier study by this project is available as evidence on lineup role coverage, its separability from talent, or talent control in this data.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether organizer, shaper, or terminal roles have a validated operational definition in this project.
Whether any prior analysis of these roles, their reliability, or their talent adjustment has been run or failed.
Whether the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data supports a stable role measure across seasons.
own_inferences: The data (play-by-play, substitutions, starters, box score, derived play-type possessions) appears sufficient to compute lineup-level role coverage counts for 90 team-seasons, so the question is not blocked by missing raw data.

The question as posed does not define 'organizer', 'shaper', or 'terminal' in terms of the data fields, and 'talent control behaves' is not a testable criterion until it is specified. These must be fixed before analysis.

Coverage is likely strongly correlated with minutes and with the talent of the players who fill roles, so separability from talent and counts is the central difficulty and may be only weakly identified.
If roles are derived from play-type records that include points, coverage will be partly constructed from the outcome that is later modeled, which creates a circularity risk.
The unit count (420,993 possessions) is large, but lineup-level cells with multiple role combinations are likely sparse, so within-team power for role-specific effects is probably limited.
uncertainties: No historical records were available, so the reliability of role labels and talent proxies is unknown.
The glossary and data catalog were not consulted, so the exact fields used to define roles and talent were not verified.
The 2025-26 playoffs and regular season are partial before the stated completion dates; the data version and cutoff must be fixed.
The number of lineups per team-season and the distribution of minutes per lineup are not known.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned no records, so no earlier finding, failed approach, or prior work changed the decision. The decision rests on the task statement and the data description alone.

blocking_constraints.text: Roles are built from derived play-type records that include points; coverage must be defined without outcome information from the same possessions being modeled.
Lineup-level role combinations are likely sparse within a team-season, limiting power for within-team coverage effects.
Coverage is likely collinear with minutes and player talent, so separability from talent and counts may not be identified.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so it is unknown whether this question has been answered in this project.

risks.text: Role labels derived from play-type records that carry points can leak the outcome into the coverage measure, inflating apparent effects of coverage on performance.
Role coverage computed from the full season may use possessions that occur after the outcome being predicted; coverage must be measured on a strictly prior window.
Talent, minutes, and role assignment are correlated; without an external or pre-season talent measure, coverage effects cannot be separated from talent.
Many lineups have few possessions; role-combination cells may be empty or tiny within a team-season.
Role classifications from play-type labels may be unstable across seasons and across partial versus complete data, so reliability of the coverage measure is unknown.
Automated play-type initiator and type labels may misclassify roles, so role coverage may reflect labeling noise.
With 90 team-seasons, between-team power is limited; within-team tests depend on lineup-level counts that may be too few.
Three roles, several talent proxies, and multiple season slices create many comparisons without a fixed analysis plan.
Role usage and play-type tagging can change across 2022-23 to 2025-26; pooling seasons may mix definitions.
If coverage is uniformly high or low across lineups, within-team variation may be too small to test.

design.estimand: Within-team association between lineup role coverage (at least one organizer, shaper, or terminal on court) and lineup possession-level outcome, after adjustment for talent proxies and minutes, with coverage shown to be separable from those covariates.
design.unit: Lineup-possession or lineup-stint within team-season, with team-season as the grouping level for variance estimation.
design.sample: Regular-season NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 (2025-26 only after the stated completion date, 2026-04-13); playoffs as a separate, pre-declared stratum. Possessions only from lineups with a minimum pre-specified count.
design.power: Compute the minimum detectable within-team coverage effect before analysis using simulated lineup counts; state the threshold and treat underpowered lineup cells as inconclusive rather than null.
design.controls: Talent proxies fixed before analysis (for example pre-season or prior-season box-score ratings), minutes/exposure counts, team and season fixed effects; coverage defined from play-type fields excluding points; coverage computed only from possessions strictly before the outcome window.
design.falsification: Pre-specify a placebo role (role absent from the lineup set) and a placebo season; a coverage effect that persists under placebo labels or disappears under talent adjustment is an artifact, not support.
design.multiplicity: Single primary contrast (any-role coverage) pre-registered; secondary role-specific contrasts reported with a correction for the number of roles and seasons.
design.decision_rule: Support requires the primary contrast to exceed the pre-specified minimum detectable effect, to survive talent and minutes adjustment, and to hold under placebo and season splits. Reject if an adequately powered test shows no coverage effect after adjustment. Report uncertain if power or reliability criteria are not met.
design.data_version: Frozen data snapshot with the regular season 2025-26 marked complete only from 2026-04-13 and playoffs 2025-26 complete only from 2026-06-21; record the version and cutoff date in the registration.

methodological_questions: Is lineup role coverage separable from player talent and minutes counts?
Does talent control behave adequately when coverage is measured per lineup and per team-season?
What exposure, reliability, and derived-label risks affect role coverage measures?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
